info.title: ModernWeather management API
info.description: The management API over ConfigAdmin and ComponentControl. GENERATED from the Rust handlers in crates/mw-api-mgmt by `cargo xtask mgmt-schema`. DO NOT EDIT. Every route is /api/v1/* (DESIGN.md D-49); the frozen public contract is unversioned and is not described here (D-37).

post.description:
**Revokes every other session and keeps this one**, which is implementation-plan.md
**M7-2**'s done-criterion and what a person expects after "my laptop was stolen". The
cookie is therefore *not* cleared and no new session is minted: the operator stays on
the page they were on.

author should read them.

get.description:
Its own resource rather than `/services/aerisweather`, and the reason is §4.4's: an
account with a client-id pair and a station list has no field in common with an upload
account's interval, endpoint and APRS symbols, so one union would be an object with every
field optional. §1.4's mapping is honoured by the *page*, which is one page under "Share
my data" either way.

§1.3 notes that the Go surface has no by-id read for storage while weather stations and
websites have one, and that the new surface removes the inconsistency. It removes it by
**having** the route rather than by pretending there can be two.

put.description:
A connection the database **rejects** is still a legitimate save (§7.2): the database may
be down or about to be reconfigured, so the save succeeds, `db:postgres` moves to
`Backoff`, and §2.4's banner ⑤ reports it. Conflating "I can't reach it" with "that input
is invalid" is how a UI ends up refusing to let an operator fix a configuration while the
thing it configures is down.

delete.summary: Turn off the weather radar map and forget its registration.

Applied.description:
What a preview or a save answers with.

One type for both, because the client renders the same three things either way: whether
it is acceptable, what it does, and what it is worth knowing. §2.4's `{ "valid": true,
"diff": {...}, "warnings": [...] }` and §2.2's `{ "generation": 42, "affects": [...] }`
are the same object seen twice.

affects.description:
The ids a client watches `applied_generation` on to decide when the change is live
(§2.2). The union of `start` and `restart`: a stopped component never reports an
applied generation again, so waiting for one would wait forever.

committed.description: Whether the configuration was committed, or only tried.

diff.description: What it does to the running component set.

generation.description:
The configuration generation. On a save this is the **new** one; on a preview it is
the generation the preview was taken against, so a client can tell that the ground
moved under it.

valid.description:
Whether the configuration is acceptable. Always `true` on a `200`; a refusal is a
`422` with [`crate::error::ErrorBody`], which carries the field paths.

AuthStateView.description:
`GET /api/v1/auth/session` — the one unauthenticated read, and the first request the UI
makes.

Three states in one object, which is what §1.1 means by "also reports whether the
instance has been claimed, which drives the first-run redirect":

| `claimed` | `authenticated` | the client shows |
|---|---|---|
| `false` | `false` | §0.7's "Create your administrator account" |
| `true` | `false` | the login screen (§8.8's signed-out state) |
| `true` | `true` | the application |

`claimed = false, authenticated = true` is unrepresentable in practice and is not
special-cased: the claim creates the credential and the session in one transaction.

authenticated.description: Whether this request carried a live session.

password_policy.description: The password rule the forms should state.

oneOf.description: This request's session, when `authenticated`.

Badge.description:
The badge a state gets, as §0.4's table names it.

Note that the badge is **not** the state's own word: `Failed` is badged **Stopped** and
`Stopped` is badged **Off**, because the only way an operator deliberately reaches
`Stopped` is by turning something off — and a red "Failed" on something they switched off
themselves is the UI lying in the other direction.
`String` rather than `&'static str`, even though every value is a literal: the badge is
deserialised by the generated TypeScript client's Rust-side counterpart in this
repository's own tests, and `Deserialize` cannot produce a `&'static str`.

Blocked.description: One thing a root cause is holding up.

Blocker.description: What is blocking a component, named as the thing it is.

href.description: Where to go to look at it, when it has a page.

provider.description: The provider's internal id, when the plan names one. For keying and deep links.

provider_display.description: What it is, on screen: "the weather database", not `ReadingStore`.

oneOf.description: Add or update a weather station.

key.description: Which station. Absent on a create, where [`StationInput::key`] carries it.

Change where this node listens.

Change.description:
Everything an operator can change, as one discriminated union.

Both `POST /api/v1/config/preview` and every mutating route construct one of these, which
is what makes the preview and the save one code path. The discriminant is `change` so
that `openapi-typescript` emits a union the client narrows on rather than an object with
every field optional.

channels.description: The channels this connection should receive from now on.

ChannelsView.description: What a channel change answers with.

channels.description: The channels now in force, which is what the client asked for when it succeeded.

password_again.description: The same password again (§3.4 step 3: "a password (twice)").

setup_code.description:
The code printed to the console at first start.

Secret for the same reason the password is, and for one more: this is the value
§3.5's "nothing secret in logs" rule makes the single deliberate exception for, and
the exception is the **banner**, not a `{:?}`.

applied_generation.description:
The generation the **running instance** was built from (**D-53**).

Per component, not global: a global "configuration version applied" would be wrong
the moment one component restarts and another does not, which is the common case,
since unchanged components are deliberately not touched.

badge.description:
The badge §0.4 gives that state. Note that it is not the state's own word: `failed`
is badged **Stopped** and `stopped` is badged **Off**.

degraded.description:
Which soft requirements are unavailable, as things. Empty is the ordinary case — and
a degraded component **is running and serving** (W2a Decision 27).

display.description: What it is called on screen — the server does the translation, once (**D-36**).

id.description:
The internal id. **Never rendered raw** outside `System → Advanced`; it travels for
keying, deep links and support.

last_error.description: The last error, with its full cause chain (**D-34**), for the Details disclosure.

notes.description: §0.4's counter sentences, each already filtered by its own "shown when" condition.

pending.description:
Whether this component is still catching up with the change that was just saved.

§2.2's derived fact, computed here as well as being computable by the client: the
comparison is the whole mechanism, and a server that reports the integers but not
their relation invites five clients to re-derive it five ways.

**Scoped to the components the newest change affects** ([`Awaiting`]), not to every
component below the newest generation. An unchanged component is deliberately not
touched, so it is not behind -- it was never asked to move.

retry_at.description:
When the next retry happens, for a `backoff` state.

An **absolute timestamp**, because W5 **D-46** makes the only client-side timer a
countdown rendering one of these: a server-supplied "12 seconds" is wrong by the time
it is painted.

sentence.description: The sentence §0.4 gives that state, in the operator's words.

since.description: Since when it has been in this state.

waiting_on.description: What it is waiting for, as things rather than capabilities.

ComponentsView.description: §2.3's resource: every component, and the newest committed generation.

components.description: Every component in the plan, in id order.

ConfigView.description:
The whole configuration, with every secret omitted.

`GET /api/v1/config` under `System → Advanced` only (§1.10). No ordinary screen fetches
this; the per-resource routes are projections of it.

oneOf.description: Forecasts and alerts, if an account is configured.

generation.description:
The newest committed configuration generation (**D-53**). The integer every screen
compares a component's `applied_generation` against.

oneOf.description: This node, if it has started before. `None` is a first start.

services.description: Every upload service that has an account row.

stations.description: Every weather station, including the disabled ones.

oneOf.description: The weather database, if one is configured.

lagged_total.description: Readings this component was too slow to receive.

misfired_total.description: Scheduled occurrences missed while the daemon was not running.

restart_total.description: Times this component has been rebuilt.

runs_total.description: Occurrences that ran, whatever the outcome.

skipped_total.description: Occurrences skipped because the previous one was still going.

stop_timeout_total.description: Stops that had to be forced.

Counts.description: How many components are in each state.

Credential.description:
Whether a credential is stored, which is the only thing any endpoint says about one.

A unit-like struct rather than a bare `bool` so that the schema -- and therefore the
generated TypeScript -- carries the reason, and so that a field of this type cannot be
confused with a feature toggle by a reader of either side.

is_set.description: Whether something is stored. Never what.

Display.description: What a component is called on screen.

name.description: What it is: "Weather Underground", "Saving readings", "your Davis station".

qualifier.description: Which station or website it belongs to, when it belongs to one.

section.description: Which part of the UI owns it.

EnrolmentToken.description:
One outstanding or historical enrolment token.

W7 D-33, as W5 is required to surface it: **leaving enrolment open is the mistake and
it should be visible.** `Enroll` is served only while an unexpired, unconsumed token
exists, so an outstanding row is a door that is open right now.

consumed_at.description: When it was consumed, if it was.

id.description:
The row's id, hex. Never the token: the row holds an Argon2id hash and the
plaintext was printed once.

peer_name.description: Which peer it was minted for.

state.description: `outstanding`, `used` or `expired` -- the three states the row can be in.

EnrolmentView.description: Outstanding enrolment and the history behind it.

log.description:
Every token this node has minted, newest first -- the enrolment log.

The log and the outstanding list come from the same rows rather than from a
separate audit table, and that is a property worth stating: a history assembled
from a different source than the live state is a history that can disagree with it.

outstanding.description: Tokens that would admit a new peer **right now**.

ErrorBody.description:
The management API's error body.

`summary` is the one plain line a banner shows when there is no field to attach to;
`detail` is the technical half, which W5 §0.4 puts behind a **Details** disclosure rather
than on the screen. Both are present on every error so the client never has to decide
which one it got.

detail.description: The technical cause chain, for the disclosure. Empty when there is nothing more.

errors.description: Per-field problems, when the request's *values* are what is wrong.

summary.description: One plain sentence, for a banner.

FieldError.description:
One problem with one field of a submitted form.

`field` is a **path** into the request body -- `stations[0].hostname`, `interval_seconds`
-- because that is what lets the client put the message beside the input. `message` is in
the operator's words and says what to type (§0.1): "Enter a hostname or IP address.", not
"invalid hostname".

field.description: Where in the submitted body the problem is.

message.description: What is wrong, as a sentence that says what to do.
message.example: Enter a hostname or IP address.

FleetView.description:
What `GET /api/v1/fleet` returns.

An object whose three members are each nullable, rather than three routes, because the
two pages that render it show all three together and §4.4 wants one object with named
fields so a fourth number is additive.

oneOf.description: Enrolment, which is `None` on a node that is not a collector.
The unsent-readings buffer, or `None` on a node that has none.

ForecastsInput.description: Forecasts and alerts, as their page submits them.

client_secret.description: A new client secret. Omit to keep the stored one.

enabled.description: Whether to fetch forecasts and alerts.

refresh_interval_seconds.description: How often to refresh, in seconds.

stations.description: Which stations get forecasts and alerts.

ForecastsView.description:
"Forecasts & alerts" — the Aeris account, named as a detail and not as the feature
(§0.2).

api_endpoint.description: An endpoint override. `None` is the vendor's.

client_id.description: The account's client id, which is not a secret on its own.

client_secret.description: Whether the client secret is stored.

enabled.description: Whether forecasts and alerts are being fetched.

refresh_interval_seconds.description: How often forecasts are refreshed, in seconds. `None` is the derived span/4.

stations.description: Which stations get forecasts and alerts.

LatestReading.description:
One station's latest reading, as the Home tiles and §0.7 step 3 render it.

A handful of named fields rather than the 212-column reading: these are the ones §0.7's
panel shows, and widening it later is additive under §4.4. The units are in the field
names because the frozen contract's are, and a unit carried in a name cannot be
converted twice.

station_key.description: Which station, by the key every path segment uses.

station_name.description:
What the operator calls it, so the tile needs no second lookup.

Filled in by the stream from the vocabulary, **not** by the implementation of
[`Readings`]: D-36 puts the translation on the server in one place, and the half of
the system that produces readings has no business knowing what a station is called.
An implementation may leave it empty.

ts.description: When the station says it measured.

ListenerInput.description: Where this node listens, as `System → Advanced` submits it.

listen_addr.description: The address the public site binds.

ListenerView.description:
"Website & API" plus `System → Advanced`: where this node listens.

The `management` controller gets no page of its own (§1.4) — it is the thing the operator
is looking at. Its address, port and certificate are here, where changing the port shows
the warning and the new URL; its `auth_token` does not exist under §3.

grpc_port.description: The "App & integration port" (§0.2) — where the phone app connects.

https_port.description: The public HTTPS port, when one is configured. `Some` makes the HTTP port a redirect.

listen_addr.description: The address the public site binds.

management_bound_addr.description:
The address it is **actually** bound to.

Not always [`ListenerView::management_listen_addr`]: until implementation-plan.md
**M7-2** there is no authentication, so a configured non-loopback address is narrowed
to `127.0.0.1`. Reported rather than left to the log, because §1.4's "changing the
port shows the new URL" is only honest if the URL is where the API is.

management_listen_addr.description: The address this API binds. Loopback by default (**A-W5-3**).

management_tls_cert_path.description:
This API's certificate.

A **path**, not a credential, so it is returned — and it has to be, for
[`StationView::aprs_callsign`]'s reason: a form that cannot prefill it writes `NULL`
back, and an unrelated port change would silently turn off TLS on this API.

LogEntry.description:
One log entry, already rendered.

`message` is the formatted event and `causes` is its chain, rendered at the point it was
recorded (**D-34**) rather than reconstructed here. `fields` is flattened to strings
because the log view shows them and does not compute on them — and because a `Value`
union in the schema would make the generated TypeScript a tagged union the log table has
no use for.

fields.description: Its structured fields, in the order the event recorded them.

spans.description:
The spans it happened inside, outermost first. This is what makes per-station
filtering possible at all (§5.4).

stream.description:
Which ring it came from: `app` or `access`.

W3 §5.7 keeps the two **rings** separate -- its eviction-asymmetry argument holds --
and §1.8 merges the *presentation*, because correlating a 500 with the query that
failed is the whole job.

LogField.description:
One structured field on a log entry.

A named pair rather than a `(String, String)` tuple or a map, and each alternative is
rejected for its own reason: a tuple becomes a positional array in the schema, which is a
shape with no name on either side of the wire, and a map loses the order the event
recorded its fields in -- which is the order the log table shows them in.

directive.description: The directive to install, or `null` to go back to the one the process started with.

The filter directive in force, in `RUST_LOG` syntax.

Carried verbatim and **not** translated: a person turning on debug logging for one
station is reading documentation that uses this syntax, which is §0.3's test applied
to a field only that person sees.

password.description:
Their password.

A `SecretString` from the moment it is deserialised (**D-33**, §3.2), so a `{:?}` on
this struct anywhere downstream cannot print it. `value_type = String` because that
is what is on the wire; the schema describes the JSON, not the Rust.

LogsView.description: What a read of the log rings returns.

dropped.description:
How many entries the ring has evicted since the process started.

§0.4 renders this as the **gap marker** in the log view rather than as a number in a
corner: "{n} log entries dropped" belongs where the gap is, because that is the
question it answers.

Named.description:
A thing the configuration names, in the words a screen uses.

Returned beside a change so that the **server** renders the vocabulary once (§2.3) rather
than every client doing it: `display.section` and `display.href` are what let the UI link
a consequence to the page that owns it without knowing the component model.

display.description: What it is called on screen.

href.description: Where to go to see it.

id.description:
The internal id. Travels for keying, deep links and support; rendered raw only inside
`System → Advanced` (**D-36**).

section.description: Which part of the UI owns it.

node_id.description: The node's identity, as a UUID string.

spool_max_lag_seconds.description: How far behind the spool is allowed to get, in seconds.

timezone.description: The deployment time zone, for components not scoped to a station.

PairingInput.description: One station a service is turned on for.

remote_station_id.description: That station's identifier at the far end.

PairingView.description: One station this service is turned on for.

remote_station_id.description:
That station's identifier at the far end -- a Weather Underground or PWS Weather
station id. A property of the pairing, not of the account.

current_password.description:
The current password. **Required** (§3.5): a session is not sufficient authority to
replace the credential, because the session is what a borrowed laptop has.

PasswordPolicyView.description:
The password rule, so the form states it rather than restating it.

§0.5's inline-help standard applied to the one rule there is: a client that hardcoded
"at least 12 characters" would be a second copy of [`crate::auth::POLICY_MIN_CHARS`],
and the two would disagree the first time the policy moved.

last_seen.description: When it was last heard from.

name.description: The peer's name, as it enrolled.

node_id.description: Its node id, hex, shown only under `System → Advanced`.

peer_reported_depth_envelopes.description:
W7 D-40's `IngestBatch.sender_depth`: how many readings the **peer says** it still
has unsent.

**Peer-reported, and the field name says so**, because W7 D-40 requires W5 to label
it as such wherever it appears and a field called `depth` would make that a
convention the next page could forget. It is what lets this node render fleet-wide
lag without scraping a satellite whose link is down -- and it is the satellite's
own claim, not a measurement.

revoked_at.description:
When its enrolment was revoked, if it was.

Revocation is a timestamp rather than a deletion precisely so that "this peer was
trusted until Tuesday" is readable off this page -- so a view that dropped it would
render a refused peer as a working one, which is the most expensive direction for a
fleet page to be wrong in.

stations.description: Which stations it has registered, by key.

PlanOutline.description:
What a change does to the running component set.

§2.4's `diff`, with one difference in naming that is worth being explicit about:
`PlanDiff`'s words are `added`/`removed`/`changed`, and this resource's are
`start`/`stop`/`restart`, because those are what the operator is being asked to agree to.
`unchanged` is a **count** rather than a list for the same reason — twenty-seven things
not happening is one fact.

restart.description: Things whose configuration changed, which are stopped and started again.

start.description: Things that do not exist yet and will.

stop.description: Things that exist and will not.

unchanged.description:
How many are left exactly as they are. **Not touched** — which is what makes "saving
a website no longer disturbs the APRS schedule" observable rather than asserted.

RadarInput.description: A radar registration, as "Turn on the weather radar map" submits it.

token.description: The token the registration returned. Write-only: no response returns it (§1.5).

to_generation.description: Which generation to go back to. One step only, and only within this process's life.

RootCause.description: One underlying problem, and everything waiting on it.

blocking.description: Everything that is waiting on this, directly or through something else.

detail.description: The technical half, for the Details disclosure.

message.description: One plain sentence: "Can't connect to the weather database. Retrying in 12 seconds."

retry_at.description: When the next retry happens, for the client's countdown (**D-46**).

unaffected_note.description:
What is **still working**, when anything is.

Not reassurance padding: W3 §2a.6's measured result is that `/latest` is served from
the in-memory snapshot and is untouched by a database outage, and this is exactly the
thing an operator cannot currently determine during an incident. Computed from the
listener's and the frozen surface's actual states rather than asserted, so it cannot
claim the website is up while it is down.

ScheduleView.description:
One component's schedule state.

**Real, not inferred.** W2a §1.3 puts the clock in the supervisor, so these are state;
today they are local variables inside `for { select { case <-ticker.C: } }` loops and are
not observable at all.

kind.description:
The trigger's kind: `Every`, `Calendar`, `OnReading`, `OnStartup`, `Service`,
`OnDemand`. Internal vocabulary, carried for the Advanced view and for keying; the
sentence beside it is what a screen renders (**D-36**).

period_s.description: The period in seconds, where the trigger has one.

sentence.description:
The sentence: "Runs every 10 minutes." `None` for `OnDemand`, which is a button
rather than a schedule (§0.4).

Section.description:
Which part of the UI owns a thing.

§2.3's list exactly. A closed enum rather than a string because the client switches on
it to choose a navigation group, and a typo would be a silently unreachable screen.

SerialPort.description: One serial port the operator can pick.

description.description:
What it is, if the kernel says: "FTDI FT232R USB UART". Shown beside the path,
because `/dev/ttyUSB0` and `/dev/ttyUSB1` are indistinguishable without it.

stable_device.description:
A stable path that survives a reboot, where the kernel offers one.

Offered because `/dev/ttyUSB0` is assigned in probe order: a Pi with a console and a
TNC plugged in swaps them across a reboot, and the station silently reads the wrong
device. The picker defaults to this where it exists.

ServiceInput.description: One upload service, as its page submits it — the account and its stations together.

api_key.description: A new API key. Omit to keep the stored one.

interval_seconds.description: How often it uploads, in seconds. Omit for the service's default.

name.description: The account's name, which is the stable suffix of its component ids.

passcode.description: A new APRS passcode. Omit to keep the stored one.

stations.description: Which stations this service is on for. Replaces the whole set.

ServiceView.description:
One upload service — a page under "Share my data".

There is no "add a controller" action and no list of controllers (§1.4): creating a
service is "turn on Weather Underground for this station", which is a `PUT` to this
resource.

api_endpoint.description: An endpoint override. `None` is the vendor's.

api_key.description: Whether an API key is stored.

aprs_kiss_path.description: The digipeater path. Keeps its name (§0.3): it is the word on the licence.

display.description: What it is called on screen: "Weather Underground", "PWS Weather", "APRS / CWOP".

interval_seconds.description: How often it uploads, in seconds. `None` is the kind's default.

name.description: The account's name, which is also the stable suffix of its component ids.

passcode.description:
Whether an APRS passcode is stored. The **callsign** is on the station, because it is
public identity printed on every packet.

stations.description: Which stations this service is on for.

services.description: Every upload service that has an account.

SessionView.description: One session, as the session list shows it.

current.description:
Whether this is the session making the request, so the list can say "this browser"
rather than offering to sign the operator out of the page they are looking at.

id.description: The public handle, hex. What `DELETE /api/v1/auth/sessions/{id}` names.

user_agent.description: The browser that created it, if it said — §3.3's "which browser is this?".

SignedInView.description:
What a successful login, claim or password change answers with.

One type for all three because the client does the same thing with all three: it is
signed in, as this person, on this session, with these things worth knowing. `warnings`
is §8.5's non-blocking slot and is where **O-10**'s breached-password notice lands --
which is the whole reason that decision is "warn" rather than "refuse".

session.description: The session this request is now on.

SpoolView.description:
The unsent-readings buffer, as `/data-storage/send` renders it.

W7 specified four numbers after W5 had finished and W5's inventory therefore has none
of them. Three are here and the fourth is on [`PeerView`]:

* `time_remaining_seconds` -- W7's `spool_time_remaining_seconds`;
* the `ceiling < max_lag x rate` advisory of W7 §3.5, as the three figures it compares
  plus the comparison's result, so that the sentence is rendered by W5 §0's vocabulary
  rather than assembled from a server-side string;
* the depth, which W5 already had.

**The comparison is made here, not in the client.** It is one inequality over three
numbers, and a client that re-derives it is a second opinion about whether an operator
is about to lose data.

bytes_per_second.description:
The observed write rate, over the window this process has been running.

`None` until there is enough traffic to divide by: a rate computed from two
appends is a number that would make the advisory below oscillate.

ceiling_bytes.description: How much disk unsent readings may use before the oldest are reclaimed (W7 D-16).

ceiling_covers_max_lag.description:
Whether the ceiling covers `max_lag` at the observed rate.

`None` when there is no rate to compare against, which is **not** the same as
`true`: "we cannot tell yet" and "you are fine" are different sentences, and
collapsing them is what makes a ceiling policy a coin flip (W7 §3.5).

depth_envelopes.description: How many readings are waiting, when the buffer can say.

last_delivery.description: The last time a peer acknowledged a batch.

max_lag_seconds.description: How long a cursor may be behind before it is abandoned.

needed_for_max_lag_bytes.description: What the ceiling would have to be to cover `max_lag` at the observed rate.

path.description: Where the buffer lives, for `System → Advanced` and for a support message.

time_remaining_seconds.description:
W7's `spool_time_remaining_seconds`: how long the remaining ceiling covers at the
observed rate. `None` for the same reason as the rate.

StationInput.description: A weather station, as the "Add a station" and "Station settings" forms submit it.

aprs_callsign.description: The APRS callsign — public identity, printed on every packet.

identity_kind.description: How a frame's station identity is resolved.

key.description:
The domain identity. Required on a create and ignored on an update — the path
segment is what identifies the row, and the key is not renameable.

poll_interval_seconds.description: How often a WeatherLink Live unit is polled, in seconds.

presented_key.description: The identifier a non-`fixed` station presents.

protocol_secret.description: A new protocol secret. Omit to keep the stored one.

sensor_mapping.description: "Which sensor is which", as the resolved mapping.

snow_base_distance_mm.description: The distance a snow gauge reads with no snow under it, in millimetres.

wind_dir_correction_degrees.description: The vane's offset from north, in degrees.

StationView.description: One weather station, as a read returns it.

altitude_m.description: Metres. The column's name carries its unit so the conversion cannot be done twice.

aprs_callsign.description:
The APRS callsign — public identity, printed on every packet, which is why it is on
the station and not beside the passcode.

**Returned**, unlike every credential on this type: a form that cannot prefill it
writes `NULL` back on the next save, and `plan()` then refuses the whole
configuration while APRS is paired — a station that cannot be edited at all.

id.description:
The surrogate integer the **frozen** contract returns as `stations[].id`. Carried
here because the UI deep-links the public site, which takes `?station_id=`.

identity_kind.description:
How a frame's station identity is resolved: `fixed`, `from_path`, `from_query`,
`from_payload` or `from_registration`.

key.description:
The domain identity, and the id every path segment uses.

**Not renameable.** It is the stable suffix of this station's component ids and the
key its history is stored under, so changing it would orphan the readings in the
weather database -- a migration rather than an edit.

kind.description: The hardware type, in the frozen contract's spelling.

kind_display.description:
What the hardware type is called on screen (§0.2) -- "Snow depth sensor", not
`snowgauge`.

poll_interval_seconds.description: How often a WeatherLink Live unit is polled, in seconds.

presented_key.description: The identifier a non-`fixed` station presents.

protocol_secret.description: Whether a protocol secret is stored for this station.

sensor_mapping.description:
"Which sensor is which", as the stored mapping (§1.6). Opaque here; the picker
resolves templates client-side.

shared_with.description:
Which services this station's readings are shared with, as the service keys.

Read-only on the station page, which is **OQ-W5-4**'s resolution: the Go schema
configures the same service in two places, and the UI's answer is one page per
service plus this line, which links there.

snow_base_distance_mm.description: The distance a snow gauge reads with no snow under it, in millimetres.

timezone.description: An IANA time-zone name. `None` is a station whose day boundaries happen in UTC.

wind_dir_correction_degrees.description: The vane's offset from north, in degrees.

stations.description: Every station, including the disabled ones.

StorageInput.description: The weather database's connection, as its form submits it.

url.description: The PostgreSQL URL. A credential, so it is write-only: no response returns it.

StorageView.description:
The weather database — "Data storage" on screen, never "TimescaleDB" (§0.2).

**Its absence is meaningful**, which is why this is an `Option` on [`ConfigView`] rather
than a row with empty fields: a node with no weather database has no `db:postgres` and
therefore no `writer:timescale` (**D-44**), and the screen says so.

connection.description: Whether a connection URL is stored. It is a credential, so that is all this says.

database.description: The database name the URL names.

host.description: The host the URL names, for the screen. **Not the URL**: it carries a password.

id.description:
There is one weather database, so one id. Carried because the route is
`PUT /api/v1/storage/{id}` -- §1.3's note that the Go surface has no by-id read for
storage while stations and websites do is an inconsistency this surface removes by
*having* the by-id route, not by pretending there can be two.

SummaryView.description: §2.5's resource: the root-cause rollup Home renders.

counts.description: How many components are in each state.

health.description:
`ok`, `degraded` or `broken`.

**`broken` means the public website is not serving**, and nothing else does: that is
the one distinction an operator makes a different decision on. A failed uploader with
a healthy site is `degraded`, because the thing the owner's visitors see is up.

pending.description:
How many components have not yet caught up with [`SummaryView::generation`].

§2.4's `ApplyBanner { count }`: "Saved. 1 item is restarting…". Zero is "Saved and
live."

root_causes.description: One entry per underlying problem — not one per symptom.

pid.description: The process id, which is what an operator needs to find it in `journalctl`.

target.description: The target triple it was built for.

uptime_seconds.description: How long it has been running, in seconds.

TransportInput.description: How a station is reached, as a form submits it.

credential.description:
A transport credential. **Omit to keep the stored one**; no response ever returns it,
so treating absence as a clear would erase a working credential on every save.

kind.description:
One of `serial`, `tcp_out`, `http_out`, `grpc_out`, `mqtt_sub`, `http_in`, `udp_in`.
Omitted for a station a peer forwards readings for.

mount.description: The mount point an inbound transport listens on.

streaming.description: Whether this transport streams rather than polls.

tls_ca_path.description: The CA bundle to verify against.

url.description: The URL to poll or subscribe to.

TransportView.description:
How a station is reached, as the operator configured it.

Flat rather than a tagged union over the seven `transport_kind`s, because the form is:
W5 §0.7 step 2 shows one "How is it connected?" picker and then the fields that kind
needs, and a discriminated union would make the client reconstruct the whole object to
change the picker. The schema's own `CHECK`s are what pair a kind with its columns.

baud.description: The baud rate. Keeps its name for §0.3's reason: the person holding the cable uses it.

credential.description: Whether a transport credential is stored. Never the credential.

device.description: The serial device path. "Serial port" keeps its name on screen (§0.3).

group.description: The consumer group, where the transport has one.

kind.description:
`serial`, `tcp_out`, `http_out`, `grpc_out`, `mqtt_sub`, `http_in` or `udp_in`.
`None` is a station a peer forwards readings for -- inventory, not a component.

method.description: The HTTP method, where the transport takes one.

mount.description: The mount point an inbound transport listens on.

streaming.description: Whether this transport streams rather than polls.

tls_ca_path.description: The CA bundle this transport verifies against.

topic.description: The MQTT topic or the mount point, per kind.

url.description: The URL to poll or subscribe to.

WebsiteInput.description: A website, as its form submits it.

about_station_html.description: The "about this station" text, as HTML.

air_quality_enabled.description: Whether the air-quality panel is on.

air_quality_station_key.description: Which station the air-quality panel reads.

apple_app_id.description: The App Store id for the `apple-itunes-app` tag.

hostname.description: The hostname it is served under. `""` is the default website.

is_default_tls.description: Whether this site's certificate is the SNI fallback.

primary_station_key.description: The station the site shows when the request names none.

snow_enabled.description: Whether the snow panel is on.

snow_station_key.description: Which station the snow panel reads.

WebsiteView.description: One website, as a read returns it.

about_station_html.description: The "about this station" text. **HTML**, not plain text.

air_quality_enabled.description: Whether the air-quality panel is on.

air_quality_station_key.description: Which station the air-quality panel reads.

apple_app_id.description: The App Store id for the `apple-itunes-app` tag. Empty removes the tag.

hostname.description:
The hostname it is served under. `""` is the **default** website, which an unmatched
`Host` resolves to.

is_default_tls.description: Whether this site's certificate is the SNI fallback.

is_portal.description: Whether this is the portal -- the one website `/api/stations` answers for.

primary_station_key.description: The station the site shows when the request names none.

radar_enabled.description: Whether the weather radar map is turned on.

radar_registered_at.description:
When the radar was registered.

**The token itself is never returned** (§1.5): the screen shows "Registered on
4 March 2026" and a **Re-register** action.

snow_enabled.description: Whether the snow panel is on.

snow_station_key.description: Which station the snow panel reads.
